title: AI in Everyday Life
description: Discover how AI is already embedded in the tools you use daily — and what that means for you.

data.text: AI is not a future technology. It is already running in dozens of apps you use every day — most of the time invisibly. Before we explore deliberate AI use, it helps to recognize how much AI experience you already have.
How AI went from invisible to interactive

data.text: AI you already use every day
You interact with AI dozens of times a day without thinking about it. Here are the categories and specific examples you've likely used this week:

rows: Email spam filters, social media feeds, search rankings
Netflix, Spotify, YouTube, Amazon, TikTok For You page
Google Translate, Live Caption, phone keyboard autocomplete
Face unlock, photo tagging, voice recognition ("Hey Siri")
Bank fraud detection, credit card alerts, content moderation
Google Maps ETAs, traffic rerouting, "you may also like"

data.title: The big shift happening right now
data.text: Until 2022, AI worked silently in the background — invisible, automatic, and operated by companies. With generative AI (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini), AI became something you can talk to directly. This shift from passive-AI-consumer to active-AI-user is what this course is about.
Passive AI use vs. active AI use

headers: Passive AI use (what you've always done)
Active AI use (what this course teaches)
rows: Letting the algorithm pick your next video
Asking AI to summarize a video transcript
Having AI draft the entire email
Spam filter quietly sorting your inbox
Asking AI to categorize and prioritize your messages
Asking AI to help plan a complex trip itinerary

data.text: Why this matters for your learning

Recognizing how much AI you already use has an important psychological benefit: you are not starting from zero. You already have intuitions about what AI can and cannot do. This course takes those intuitions and turns them into deliberate, versatile skills.

The difference between someone who "uses AI sometimes" and someone with genuine AI fluency is mainly habit and intentionality — not technical skill. The tools are the same; the question is whether you reach for them deliberately or wait for the algorithm to do it for you.

data.title: The same AI, two very different uses
data.content:
Language AI powers both the Instagram caption suggestions you ignore AND the full email draft you could ask Claude to write for you.

The technology is nearly identical. The difference is: one operates in the background without your input, and one amplifies your intent because you asked clearly.

data.title: Key points
points: AI has been running invisibly in apps for over a decade
Generative AI (ChatGPT, Claude) made AI something you talk to directly
You are not starting from zero — you already have years of AI experience
The difference is moving from passive use to active, intentional use
AI fluency is a practical everyday skill anyone can develop
data.takeaway: AI fluency is now a practical everyday skill, not a specialty.

data.text: Everyday AI value grows in stages: awareness, assisted execution, and workflow integration. The most sustainable progress comes from turning occasional use into repeatable habits with clear quality checks.
